claim_1.claim: ELISA analysis of serum from 56 vaccinated individuals showed binding antibody responses were induced by BNT162b2 vaccination and were boosted after the secondary vaccination (day 21), with no gender-associated difference in antibody responses.

sources.quote: Primary vaccination induced binding antibody and neutralizing antibody responses in all but three individuals; these responses were boosted significantly after the secondary vaccination
There was no gender-associated difference in antibody responses

claim_2.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum from 56 vaccinated individuals showed neutralizing antibody responses were induced after primary vaccination (day 0), boosted significantly after the secondary vaccination (day 21), and then reduced about 2-fold by days 90–120 compared to post-boost levels.

sources.quote: Primary vaccination induced binding antibody and neutralizing antibody responses in all but three individuals; these responses were boosted significantly after the secondary vaccination
The neutralizing antibody response reduced about 2-fold by days 90–120

comparison.finding: neutralizing antibody responses were boosted significantly after the secondary vaccination compared to after primary vaccination
neutralizing antibody responses were reduced about 2-fold by day 90 compared to post-boost levels
neutralizing antibody responses were reduced about 2-fold by day 120 compared to post-boost levels

claim_3.claim: Neutralizing Antibody Titer Assay analysis of serum from 30 vaccinated individuals showed a neutralizing antibody response against the B.1.351 variant, but at a tenfold-lower magnitude than against the wild-type WA1/2020 strain.

sources.quote: BNT162b2 vaccination also induced a neutralizing antibody response against the B.1.351 variant of concern, albeit at a tenfold-lower magnitude than against the wild-type WA1/2020 (WA1) strain

claim_4.claim: Flow Cytometry analysis of PBMCs from vaccinated individuals showed spike-specific T cell responses were more readily detectable seven days after the secondary immunization (day 28) compared to earlier time points, with CD4 T cell responses primarily of the T-helper-1 type and IFNγ and TNF as the dominant CD8 T cell responses.

sources.quote: Vaccination also stimulated spike-specific T cell responses, which were more readily detectable seven days after the secondary immunization
the CD4 T cell responses were primarily of the T-helper-1 type, although there was a low-level T-helper-2 (IL-4) response
IFNγ and TNF were the dominant responses in CD8 T cells

claim_5.claim: Luminex xMAP analysis of serum from 31 vaccinated individuals on days 0, 21 and 42 showed pre-existing autoantibodies were present in five individuals, anticytokine antibodies were largely absent or low, and levels of pre-existing autoantibodies or anticytokine antibodies did not change in response to vaccination compared to baseline.

sources.quote: We screened sera of 31 vaccinated individuals for IgG autoantibodies and anticytokine antibodies on days 0, 21 and 42 using a 55-plex antigen and 58-plex cytokine arrays.
Five vaccinated individuals had pre-existing autoantibodies
Anticytokine antibodies were largely absent or were observed at a low mean fluorescence intensity with no significant changes

Importantly, none of the individuals with pre-existing autoantibodies or anticytokine antibodies experienced adverse events, nor did levels of pre-existing autoantibodies or anticytokine antibodies change in response to vaccination.

comparison.finding: levels of pre-existing autoantibodies and anticytokine antibodies did not change in response to vaccination compared to baseline; anticytokine antibodies were largely absent or low
levels of pre-existing autoantibodies and anticytokine antibodies did not change in response to vaccination compared to baseline; anticytokine antibodies were largely absent or low

claim_6.claim: CyTOF analysis of whole blood from 27 individuals showed the frequency of intermediate monocytes (CD14+CD16+ monocytes) increased significantly two days after the primary vaccination (day 2) and was substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination (day 23) compared to earlier time points.

sources.quote: The frequency of intermediate monocytes (CD14+CD16+ monocytes) increased significantly two days after the primary vaccination, and was substantially higher two days after the secondary vaccination

comparison.finding: frequency of intermediate monocytes (CD14+CD16+ monocytes) was substantially higher at day 23 than at earlier time points, following a significant increase at day 2

claim_7.claim: CyTOF analysis of whole blood from 27 individuals showed enhanced levels of phosphorylated STAT3 and STAT1 in multiple cell types on day 1 after secondary vaccination (day 22) relative to day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1).

sources.quote: there were enhanced levels of phosphorylated (p)STAT3 and pSTAT1 in multiple cell types on day 1 after secondary vaccination, relative to day 1 after primary vaccination

comparison.finding: enhanced levels of phosphorylated STAT3 and STAT1 in multiple cell types on day 22 relative to day 1

claim_8.claim: Olink analysis of plasma from 31 vaccinated individuals showed IFNγ and CXCL10 increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination (days 1 and 2), and these cytokines increased even further after the secondary immunization (day 21), with plasma IFNγ 11.3-fold higher at day 22 than at day 1 and CXCL10 peaking on day 23.

sources.quote: Of the 67 cytokines detected, the concentration of 2 cytokines (IFNγ and CXCL10) were increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination
the concentrations of these cytokines were increased even further after the secondary immunization
The concentration of plasma IFNγ was 11.3-fold higher at day 22 relative to day 1
CXCL10 peaked on day 23

comparison.finding: IFNγ and CXCL10 increased significantly on days 1 and 2 after primary vaccination
plasma IFNγ was 11.3-fold higher at day 22 than at day 1
IFNγ and CXCL10 increased even further after the secondary immunization, with IFNγ elevated at day 22
IFNγ and CXCL10 increased even further after the secondary immunization, with CXCL10 peaking on day 23

claim_9.claim: SIMOA analysis of plasma from vaccinated individuals showed IFNα2 was not significantly increased on days 1 and 2 after vaccination compared to baseline, and responses were just over the assay limit of 16 fg ml−1.

sources.quote: The concentration of IFNα2 (type I interferon) was not significantly increased on days 1 and 2 after vaccination, and the responses were just over the assay limit of the highly sensitive single-molecule array (SIMOA) (16 fg ml−1)

comparison.finding: IFNα2 was not significantly increased on day 1 compared to baseline, and responses were just over the assay limit of 16 fg ml−1
IFNα2 was not significantly increased on day 2 compared to baseline, and responses were just over the assay limit of 16 fg ml−1

claim_10.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of whole blood from 31 participants showed secondary vaccination (day 21) generated a greater transcriptional response, with nearly a fourfold increase of differentially expressed genes at day 22 compared to day 1 after primary vaccination.

sources.quote: Secondary vaccination generated a greater transcriptional response (as has previously been seen in a recent study of adjuvanted hepatitis B vaccine17), with nearly a fourfold increase of differentially expressed genes at day 22 as compared to day 1

comparison.finding: secondary vaccination generated a greater transcriptional response, with nearly a fourfold increase of differentially expressed genes at day 22 compared to day 1 after primary vaccination

claim_11.claim: Bulk RNA-seq analysis of whole blood from 31 participants showed both doses of BNT162b2 stimulated antiviral and interferon response modules, whereas secondary vaccination additionally increased signatures of dendritic cell activation and upregulated Toll-like receptor signalling, monocyte and neutrophil modules on days 22 and 23 compared to baseline.

sources.quote: Gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed that both doses of BNT162b2 stimulated antiviral and interferon response modules
secondary vaccination led to increases in signatures of dendritic cell activation and the upregulation of Toll-like receptor signalling, monocyte and neutrophil modules on days 22 and 23

comparison.finding: secondary vaccination additionally increased signatures of dendritic cell activation and upregulated Toll-like receptor signalling, monocyte and neutrophil modules on day 22 compared to baseline; both doses stimulated antiviral and interferon response modules

secondary vaccination additionally increased signatures of dendritic cell activation and upregulated Toll-like receptor signalling, monocyte and neutrophil modules on day 23 compared to baseline; both doses stimulated antiviral and interferon response modules

claim_12.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs from 6 individuals showed cluster C8 emerged on day 22, one day after secondary vaccination (day 21), expressed interferon-stimulated genes including WARS, GBP1, IFI30 and IFITM3, and increased almost 100-fold to about 1% from about 0.01% of the Lin−HLA-DR+ population compared to day 1 after primary vaccination.

sources.quote: Notably, cluster C8 (which expressed CD14, VCAN, CD1C, FCGR1A and CD274 mRNA or protein) emerged on day 22, one day after secondary vaccination
These cells uniquely expressed interferon-stimulated genes, including WARS (also known as WARS1), GBP1, IFI30 and IFITM3
constituted about 0.01% of the Lin−HLA-DR+ population on day 1 after primary vaccination but increased almost 100-fold to about 1% one day after secondary vaccination

comparison.finding: cluster C8 emerged on day 22, expressed interferon-stimulated genes WARS, GBP1, IFI30 and IFITM3, and increased almost 100-fold from about 0.01% to about 1% of the Lin−HLA-DR+ population compared to day 1
cluster C8 emerged on day 22, one day after secondary vaccination

claim_13.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs showed C8 subclusters closer to CD14+ monocytes and cDC2 expressed higher interferon-stimulated genes and reduced AP-1 transcription factors FOS and JUN compared to their parent clusters.

sources.quote: We analysed subclusters C8_1 and C8_2, which are closer to CD14+ monocytes and cDC2, respectively. In addition to expressing higher interferon-stimulated genes as compared to their parent clusters, they had a reduced expression of the AP-1 transcription factors FOS and JUN

claim_14.claim: CITE-seq analysis of PBMCs showed the interferon signature was broadly induced across cell types on day 1 after primary vaccination (day 1) and day 1 after secondary vaccination (day 22), with the higher magnitude of response on day 22.

sources.quote: our CITE-seq analysis demonstrated that the interferon signature was broadly induced across cell types on day 1 and day 22, and the higher magnitude of response on day 22 was more evident

comparison.finding: the interferon signature was broadly induced across cell types at both day 1 and day 22, with higher magnitude of response on day 22

claim_15.claim: Q-PCR analysis of purified monocytes showed in vitro stimulation with IFNγ or day-22 plasma induced a C8 signature compared to unstimulated or day-0 plasma conditions, supporting a role for IFNγ in inducing cluster C8.

sources.quote: In vitro stimulation of purified healthy monocytes with IFNγ or day-22 plasma also induced a C8 signature, which suggests that IFNγ has a key role in inducing cluster C8, in response to mRNA vaccination
